name: High-Speed Electric Device
description: Any device with a motor over 750 watts that can go faster than 28 mph and isn't registered for the road, such as an unplated e-moto or an over-limit e-bike; it can't be ridden anywhere public.

restrictions.rule: A motor exceeding 750 W and capable of speeds over 28 mph
restrictions.citation: Hawaii Revised Statutes §291C-1, as amended by HB 2021 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Excludes a moped or motor vehicle registered for public roads, a motor vehicle exempt from registration, and an electric vehicle as defined in the state energy law
restrictions.citation: Hawaii Revised Statutes §291C-1, as amended by HB 2021 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Not an electric bicycle, even with pedals
restrictions.citation: Hawaii Revised Statutes §291C-1, as amended by HB 2021 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Can't be operated on any public roadway, street, highway, bike lane, bicycle facility, travel path, sidewalk or other public area
Operating one there is a traffic infraction; for a rider under 18, enforcement may fall on the parent or guardian or take the form of non-monetary corrective action
Police and county finance officers may seize one ridden in violation of state law
